premises.text: Childhood obesity is parents' top concern, yet adult weight-loss tools are unsafe for kids because they use calorie counting
premises.evidence_span: none of these are safe for children. They all involve calorie counting, and kids are not supposed to calorie count

premises.text: Stanford Pediatric Obesity Center methods work but cost $3,500 with weekday sessions that exclude working parents
premises.evidence_span: it's $3,500 and has weekday afternoon sessions, so completely not available for working parents

premises.text: Curbo is a licensed, mobile, scalable version of the Stanford approach
premises.evidence_span: we licensed the Stanford program, and we created a mobile, scalable version of their approach

premises.text: Kids track red/yellow/green foods by nutrition value with gradually tightening goals instead of calories
premises.evidence_span: Rather than tracking calories, we have you track your red, yellow, and green foods

premises.text: Avatar choice, challenges, therapy-informed progress, and personalized avatar feedback reinforce healthier habits
premises.evidence_span: Research shows that if kids pick their avatar, they're much more likely to pay attention to the advice that it gives them

premises.text: Weekly coach calls (phone, Skype, or text) give specific feedback and remove the food-police role from parents
premises.evidence_span: taking the role of the food police away from the parents and putting it into our system

premises.text: Free food tracker attracts users; paid text messaging ($35/mo) and live coaching ($85/mo) monetize
premises.evidence_span: We're giving a free food tracker so that we can attract as many kids as we can

premises.text: Scale through insurers, hospital systems, and educational PE/nutrition classrooms
premises.evidence_span: we are talking to health insurers like Humana and UnitedHealthcare
